title: Classification of Living Things
seo_title: Life Sciences 11: Classification of Living Things Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Organisms are grouped based on common characteristics: taxonomy, binomial nomenclature, the three domains and the kingdoms, dichotomous keys and phylogenetic trees. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Life Sciences 11)
meta_desc: Free Life Sciences 11 worksheets (BC Curriculum): taxonomy, domains and kingdoms. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Living things are grouped by shared features.
key_sub: Domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.
body_html:
How to think about it

Taxonomy groups organisms from broad to specific: domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species. Each species has a two-part scientific name (binomial nomenclature), such as Ursus americanus, the black bear.

The three domains are Bacteria, Archaea and Eukarya. Eukarya includes protists, fungi, plants and animals. Phylogenetic trees show how groups are related through common ancestors; DNA evidence is now used to classify organisms.

Example

In Oncorhynchus nerka (sockeye salmon), what is the genus?

The first, capitalized word

Answer: Oncorhynchus

Example

Which domain contains organisms whose cells have a nucleus?

Eu- = true nucleus

Answer: Eukarya

Common mistakes

  • Capitalizing the species name.
  • Thinking fungi are plants.
  • Thinking organisms in the same order are more closely related than those in the same genus.

faq.a: Common names vary between languages and places; scientific names are the same everywhere.

faq.q: What does a dichotomous key do?
faq.a: It identifies an organism by a series of two-choice questions.

A quadrat survey found: species A 10, species B 5, species C 10, species D 3. Calculate Simpson's index of diversity, D = 1 − Σn(n − 1)/N(N − 1).

items.q: Which is the scientific name for pea?
items.e: Pisum sativum: pea.

items.q: Which is the scientific name for housefly?
items.e: Musca domestica: housefly.

items.q: Which category includes related orders?
items.e: e.g. Mammalia includes Primata and Carnivora.

items.q: In the hierarchy of classification, which taxon comes directly above genus?
items.e: Domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.

In the hierarchy of classification, which taxon comes directly above kingdom?
items.e: Domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.

items.q: Which is the scientific name for tiger?
items.e: Panthera tigris: tiger.

items.q: In the hierarchy of classification, which taxon comes directly below order?
items.e: Domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.

items.q: In the hierarchy of classification, which taxon comes directly below kingdom?
items.e: Domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.

items.q: In the hierarchy of classification, which taxon comes directly above phylum?
items.e: Domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.

items.q: A quadrat survey found: species A 2, species B 4, species C 10, species D 4, species E 15. Calculate Simpson's index of diversity, D = 1 − Σn(n − 1)/N(N − 1).
What is a taxon?
c: a group of organisms at any level of the hierarchy
items.e: e.g. the genus Panthera is a taxon.

items.q: What is the common name of Triticum aestivum?
items.e: Triticum aestivum: wheat.

items.q: Which is the scientific name for potato?
items.e: Solanum tuberosum: potato.

items.q: In the hierarchy of classification, which taxon comes directly below genus?
items.e: Domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.

items.q: Which organisms live in extreme habitats such as hot springs and salt marshes?
items.e: Their cell wall structure differs from other bacteria.

items.q: Which description fits kingdom Animalia?
c: prokaryotic, mostly unicellular, with a cell wall of peptidoglycan
multicellular eukaryotes with no cell wall that ingest food
heterotrophic eukaryotes with a cell wall of chitin
items.e: Animalia: multicellular eukaryotes with no cell wall that ingest food.

items.q: What is a lichen?
c: a symbiotic association of an alga and a fungus
items.e: They are pollution indicators.

items.q: Which bacteria produce methane (biogas) in the guts of cows?
items.e: They are archaebacteria.

items.q: Which taxonomic aid is a book that helps identify the species in an area?
items.e: manual: a book that helps identify the species in an area.

items.q: Who proposed the five-kingdom classification?
items.e: Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia (1969).

items.q: What is the genetic material of bacteriophages usually?
items.e: Plant viruses usually have single-stranded RNA.

items.q: Which is a living thing that cannot reproduce?
items.e: A mule is sterile.

items.q: Which is the correct order from the highest to the lowest category?
c: kingdom, class, phylum, order, family, genus, species
kingdom, phylum, order, class, family, genus, species
kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species
species, genus, family, order, class, phylum, kingdom
items.e: Remember: King Philip Came Over For Good Soup.

items.q: Which are the smallest living cells and have no cell wall?
items.e: They can survive without oxygen.

items.q: What is a botanical garden?
c: an account of the plant species found in an area
a garden of living plants grown and labelled for study
a book that helps identify the species in an area
a collection of preserved plant and animal specimens
items.e: botanical garden: a garden of living plants grown and labelled for study.

items.q: Which protists cause red tides?
items.e: They can release toxins that kill fish.

items.q: What are heterocysts in cyanobacteria used for?
items.e: e.g. Nostoc and Anabaena.

items.q: Which taxonomic aid is information about any one taxon?
items.e: monograph: information about any one taxon.

items.q: What is a manual?
c: a store of pressed, dried and labelled plant specimens on sheets
a book that helps identify the species in an area
an account of the plant species found in an area
a place where wild animals are kept in protected surroundings like their natural habitat
items.e: manual: a book that helps identify the species in an area.

items.q: What is the main drawback of the two-kingdom classification?
c: it puts prokaryotes and eukaryotes, unicellular and multicellular, together
items.e: Bacteria, fungi and plants were all in Plantae.

items.q: Which kingdom has members that are unicellular eukaryotes?
items.e: Protista: unicellular eukaryotes.

items.q: Which kingdom has members that are prokaryotic, mostly unicellular, with a cell wall of peptidoglycan?
items.e: Monera: prokaryotic, mostly unicellular, with a cell wall of peptidoglycan.

items.q: What is a key?
c: a place where wild animals are kept in protected surroundings like their natural habitat
a tool that identifies organisms using pairs of contrasting characters
a collection of preserved plant and animal specimens
items.e: key: a tool that identifies organisms using pairs of contrasting characters.

items.q: What are prions?
c: abnormally folded proteins that cause disease
items.e: e.g. mad cow disease (BSE).

items.q: Which domain includes all organisms with a nucleus?
items.e: Animals, plants, fungi and protists are eukaryotes.

items.q: What is the common name of Panthera leo?
items.e: Panthera leo: lion.

items.q: Why is DNA sequencing now used to classify organisms?
c: it is cheaper than looking at organisms
it shows relationships that are hidden by similar or different body shapes
it removes the need for names
items.e: Convergent evolution can make unrelated organisms look alike.

items.q: Which feature is best for a dichotomous key?
c: a feature that does not change, such as number of legs
the time of day the organism was seen
its colour after it has died
items.e: Use features that are fixed and easy to observe.

items.q: Which is the scientific name for human?
items.e: Homo sapiens: human.

items.q: Which is the scientific name for wheat?
items.e: Triticum aestivum: wheat.

items.q: Which is the scientific name for rice?
items.e: Oryza sativa: rice.

items.q: A horse and a donkey produce a mule, which is sterile. What does this show?
c: horses and donkeys are separate species
horses and donkeys are the same species
donkeys are a subspecies of horse
items.e: Hybrids are not fertile, so the parents are different species.

items.q: Which statement about classification is correct?
c: a class is smaller than a genus
organisms in the same kingdom are always the same species
organisms in the same genus are more closely related than organisms in the same order
items.e: Lower taxa share more features.

items.q: What is the correct order of taxa from largest to smallest?
c: domain, kingdom, class, phylum, family, order, genus, species
species, genus, family, order, class, phylum, kingdom, domain
domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species
kingdom, domain, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species
items.e: Each taxon is nested inside the one above.

items.q: What is the common name of Panthera tigris?
items.e: Panthera tigris: tiger.

items.q: In the hierarchy of classification, which taxon comes directly above class?
items.e: Domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.

items.q: What is the common name of Solanum tuberosum?
items.e: Solanum tuberosum: potato.

items.q: Why is the biological species concept hard to use for bacteria?
c: they reproduce asexually, so interbreeding cannot be tested
they are too large to study
they all belong to one species
items.e: Other concepts (genetic, morphological) are used instead.

items.q: What are the three domains of life?
items.e: The three-domain system is based on rRNA sequences.

items.q: What evidence led to the three-domain system?
c: the shape of cells under a light microscope
items.e: rRNA showed Archaea are as different from Bacteria as from eukaryotes.

items.q: Which definition of a species is used for organisms that reproduce sexually?
c: a group of organisms with the same diet
a group of organisms that look the same
a group that can interbreed in nature to produce fertile offspring
all organisms that live in one habitat
items.e: This is the biological species concept.

items.q: What does a dichotomous key do?
c: shows how energy flows through an ecosystem
lists organisms in order of size
identifies organisms by a series of choices between two features
measures the size of a population
items.e: Each step splits the group into two.

items.q: In Mangifera indica, what does 'indica' stand for?
items.e: Mangifera is the genus.

items.q: Which domain includes many organisms that live in extreme environments such as hot springs?
items.e: Archaea are prokaryotes but differ from bacteria in their membranes and rRNA.

items.q: Which population is most at risk from a new disease?
c: a small, inbred population with low genetic diversity
a large population with many alleles
a population of a widespread species
items.e: Tasmanian devils have low genetic diversity, which helped facial tumour disease spread.

items.q: Quadrats of 0.50 m² are placed at random in a 250 m² field. The mean is 2.5 buttercups per quadrat. Estimate the total number of buttercups.
What is species evenness?
c: the number of individuals of the rarest species
how similar the population sizes of the different species are
the total biomass of the community
items.e: A community where one species dominates has low evenness.

items.q: What is interspecific competition?
items.e: It can reduce the population of one species.

items.q: A quadrat divided into 50 squares has a species in 20 of them. Calculate the percentage cover (frequency).
Why is high genetic diversity important to a population?
c: some individuals are more likely to survive a new disease or change
it increases the population's size immediately
items.e: Variation is the raw material for natural selection.

items.q: A quadrat survey found: species A 12, species B 10, species C 4, species D 8. Calculate Simpson's index of diversity, D = 1 − Σn(n − 1)/N(N − 1).
A quadrat survey found: species An 8, species B 2, species C 8, species D 15. Calculate Simpson's index of diversity, D = 1 − Σn(n − 1)/N(N − 1).
What are sacred groves?
c: forest patches protected by local communities for religious reasons
items.e: Found in Meghalaya, Rajasthan, the Western Ghats and elsewhere.

items.q: Tasmanian devils have very low genetic diversity. Why has this made devil facial tumour disease worse?
c: the disease is caused by a mutation in the climate
their immune systems do not recognize tumour cells from other devils as foreign
low diversity makes them grow too fast
items.e: Similar genes mean the tumour cells are not rejected.

items.q: What does percentage cover measure?
c: the number of species in the area
the height of the tallest plant
the proportion of a quadrat's area covered by one species
the number of individuals in a quadrat
items.e: Useful for grasses and mosses that are hard to count.

items.q: What is environmental DNA (eDNA) sampling?
c: detecting species from DNA left in water or soil
items.e: eDNA can detect platypuses in a creek.

items.q: A quadrat divided into 50 squares has a species in 12 of them. Calculate the percentage cover (frequency).
What is species richness?
c: the number of different species in an area
how evenly individuals are spread among species
items.e: Richness counts species; evenness compares their numbers.

items.q: What is species diversity?
c: the variety of ecosystems in a region
the number of species in an area and how evenly the individuals are spread among them
the variety of alleles in a population
the number of individuals of one species
items.e: Species diversity takes in richness and evenness.

items.q: A quadrat survey found: species A 4, species B 5, species C 10, species D 6. Calculate Simpson's index of diversity, D = 1 − Σn(n − 1)/N(N − 1).
Two sites each have 5 species. At site An each species has about 20 individuals; at site B one species has 90 and the rest have 2 or 3. Which is more diverse?
c: they are equally diverse because richness is the same
site A, because it has the same richness and higher evenness
site B, because it has more individuals of one species
site B, because dominance means a healthier community
items.e: Same richness, higher evenness = higher diversity.

items.q: A quadrat survey found: species A 2, species B 12, species C 3. Calculate Simpson's index of diversity, D = 1 − Σn(n − 1)/N(N − 1).
When is a quadrat the best sampling method?
c: for animals that are active only at night
for plants or slow-moving animals in an area
items.e: Quadrats sample a fixed area.

c: a soft body covered by a calcareous shell and a mantle
a stomochord and proboscis gland, as in Balanoglossus
items.e: Annelida: metameric segmentation and nephridia.

c: Many new wetland species can live there.
Elk browse less by rivers, and willows and beavers return.
Mussels take over and fewer species remain.
items.e: A keystone species has a large effect.

items.q: Which animals are diploblastic?
items.e: They have only ectoderm and endoderm.

items.q: What is a pseudocoelomate?
c: an animal with no body cavity
an animal with a true coelom
an animal whose body cavity is not lined by mesoderm all round
items.e: e.g. roundworms (Aschelminthes).

items.q: Which animals show radial symmetry as adults?
items.e: Echinoderm larvae are bilaterally symmetrical.

items.q: Wolves return to Yellowstone and hunt elk. What is the most likely result?
c: Elk browse less by rivers, and willows and beavers return.
Mussels take over and fewer species remain.
Urchins increase and kelp forests shrink.
items.e: A keystone species has a large effect.

items.q: A disease kills most of the starfish on a rocky shore. What is the most likely result?
c: Mussels take over and fewer species remain.
Urchins increase and kelp forests shrink.
Many new wetland species can live there.
items.e: A keystone species has a large effect.

items.q: Which is the largest phylum of the animal kingdom?
items.e: About two-thirds of all named species are arthropods.

items.q: Which birds have pneumatic bones?
items.e: Hollow bones make them light.

items.q: Which chordates have a notochord only in the larval tail?
items.e: e.g. Ascidia and Salpa.

items.q: Which phylum shows jointed appendages and a chitinous exoskeleton?
items.e: Arthropoda: jointed appendages and a chitinous exoskeleton.

items.q: Which phylum shows metameric segmentation and nephridia?
items.e: Annelida: metameric segmentation and nephridia.

items.q: What is the excretory organ of insects?
items.e: They remove waste into the gut.

items.q: Which phylum shows comb plates and bioluminescence?
items.e: Ctenophora: comb plates and bioluminescence.

items.q: Sea otters eat sea urchins, which eat kelp. Otters disappear. What is the most likely result?
c: Mussels take over and fewer species remain.
Elk browse less by rivers, and willows and beavers return.
Urchins increase and kelp forests shrink.
items.e: A keystone species has a large effect.

items.q: Which phylum shows a soft body covered by a calcareous shell and a mantle?
items.e: Mollusca: a soft body covered by a calcareous shell and a mantle.

items.q: Which phylum shows a water vascular system and spiny skin?
items.e: Echinodermata: a water vascular system and spiny skin.
